questions.prompt: The model replies with a request to run `read_file`. What has happened to the file at that point?
options: The provider has read it and attached the contents
The model has read it but not yet summarised it
Nothing; only your program can read it, and it has not done so yet
The file has been locked until your program answers
questions.explanation: A tool call is only a request. The model runs nothing and cannot see your machine, so the file is untouched until your program acts.

questions.prompt: Why should you be careful with `function.arguments` in a tool call?
options: It is a string of JSON the model wrote token by token, so you must parse it and it may be malformed
It is encrypted with your API key
It is always an empty object
It contains the function's source code
questions.explanation: The arguments arrive as raw JSON text written by the model. You parse them yourself, and because the model wrote them, they are not guaranteed to be valid.

questions.prompt: Why is `tool_calls` a list rather than a single entry?
options: Because each argument gets its own entry
Because the provider repeats each request three times for safety
Because the list holds the tool schemas you sent
Because the model may ask for several tools in one reply, each with its own id
questions.explanation: One reply can contain several requests, for example reading two files. Each has its own id, name and arguments.
